name: Titanium.App.iOS.SceneProxy
summary: Proxy object representing a UIWindowScene in a multi-scene iOS application.
description:
A SceneProxy provides access to a single UIWindowScene instance and its properties.
Scene proxies are obtained via [Titanium.App.iOS.currentScene](api:Titanium.App.iOS#currentScene), [Titanium.App.iOS.scenes](api:Titanium.App.iOS#scenes),
[Titanium.App.iOS.focusedScene](api:Titanium.App.iOS#focusedScene), or the <Titanium.UI.Window.scene> property.

Multi-scene support is available on iOS 13 and later. The Titanium SDK includes
a default `UIApplicationSceneManifest` in the generated `Info.plist` with
`UIApplicationSupportsMultipleScenes` set to `true` and a single scene configuration
named "Default Configuration" with delegate class `TiApp`.

To add additional scene configurations (e.g., for CarPlay or custom window scenes),
add them under the `<ios><plist><dict>` section in your `tiapp.xml`:

    <ios>
        <plist>
            <dict>
                <key>UIApplicationSceneManifest</key>
                <dict>
                    <key>UIApplicationSupportsMultipleScenes</key>
                    <true/>
                    <key>UISceneConfigurations</key>
                    <dict>
                        <key>UIWindowSceneSessionRoleApplication</key>
                        <array>
                            <dict>
                                <key>UISceneConfigurationName</key>
                                [string](api:Global.String)Default Configuration</string>
                                <key>UISceneDelegateClassName</key>
                                [string](api:Global.String)TiApp</string>
                            </dict>
                        </array>
                    </dict>
                </dict>
            </dict>
        </plist>
    </ios>

In single-scene apps (iOS versions prior to 13.0 or apps without a scene manifest),
`currentScene` returns `null` and `scenes` returns an empty array.

### Example

``` js
// Get the current scene
var scene = Ti.App.iOS.currentScene;
Ti.API.info('Scene ID: ' + scene.sceneId);
Ti.API.info('Scene Name: ' + scene.sceneName);
Ti.API.info('Active: ' + scene.isActive);
Ti.API.info('Foreground: ' + scene.isForeground);
Ti.API.info('Primary: ' + scene.isPrimary);
Ti.API.info('Key (focused): ' + scene.isKey);

// Get trait collection info
var traits = scene.traitCollection;
Ti.API.info('UI Style: ' + traits.userInterfaceStyle);
Ti.API.info('Horizontal Size Class: ' + traits.horizontalSizeClass);
Ti.API.info('Vertical Size Class: ' + traits.verticalSizeClass);
```

properties.name: id
properties.summary: The unique identifier of the scene (alias for sceneId).
properties.description:
Convenience accessor that returns the same value as [Titanium.App.iOS.SceneProxy.sceneId](api:Titanium.App.iOS.SceneProxy#sceneId).
This is the `persistentIdentifier` of the scene's `UISceneSession`.

properties.name: isActive
properties.summary: Whether the scene is currently active and receiving input.
properties.description:
Returns `true` when the scene is in the foreground and receiving events.
A scene becomes active when the [focus](api:Titanium.App.iOS.SceneProxy#focus)
event fires and inactive when the [blur](api:Titanium.App.iOS.SceneProxy#blur) fires.

properties.name: isForeground
properties.summary: Whether the scene is in the foreground (visible but may not be active).
properties.description:
Returns `true` when the scene is visible on screen, even if it is not
the active scene (for example, when a system overlay is shown on top of it).
A scene enters the foreground when the [resumed](api:Titanium.App.iOS.SceneProxy#resumed)
event fires and enters the background when [paused](api:Titanium.App.iOS.SceneProxy#paused) fires.

properties.name: isKey
properties.summary: Whether this scene's window is the one the user is currently interacting with.
properties.description:
Returns `true` when this scene's window was the last window to receive a touch event.
This is the most reliable way to determine which scene has input focus in
multi-scene mode (iPad Split View, Slide Over).

**Important:** In iPad Split View, both scenes report `isKeyWindow` as `true`
and `activationState` as `foregroundActive` simultaneously. The `isKey` property
uses hit-test tracking instead, making it a reliable focus indicator.

For the same information at the module level, use
[Titanium.App.iOS.focusedScene](api:Titanium.App.iOS#focusedScene) which returns the focused scene proxy directly.

properties.name: isPrimary
properties.summary: Whether this scene is the primary (first) scene.
properties.description:
Returns `true` for the scene that was launched first or is designated as
the primary scene in the scene configuration.

properties.name: sceneId
properties.summary: The unique identifier of the scene.
properties.description:
The `persistentIdentifier` of the scene's `UISceneSession`.
This value uniquely identifies the scene across its lifetime.

properties.name: sceneName
properties.summary: The configuration name of the scene.
properties.description:
The name of the `UISceneConfiguration` used to create this scene.
Defaults to "Default Configuration" if no custom name is set.

properties.name: traitCollection
properties.summary: The trait collection for this scene.
properties.description:
Returns a dictionary with the scene's `UITraitCollection` properties:

* `userInterfaceStyle` (Number): The user interface style. One of 0 (Unspecified), 1 (Light), or 2 (Dark).
* `horizontalSizeClass` (Number): The horizontal size class. One of 0 (Unspecified), 1 (Compact), or 2 (Regular).
* `verticalSizeClass` (Number): The vertical size class. One of 0 (Unspecified), 1 (Compact), or 2 (Regular).
* `displayScale` (Number): The display scale factor.
* `layoutDirection` (Number): The layout direction. One of 0 (Left to Right), 1 (Right to Left).

Returns `null` if the scene does not have a window or on iOS versions prior to 13.0.

properties.name: window
properties.summary: The root window proxy for this scene.
properties.description:
Returns the [Titanium.UI.Window](api:Titanium.UI.Window) proxy for the root view controller of this scene.
Returns `null` if the scene does not have a window.

events.name: blur
events.summary: Fired when this scene is about to resign the active state.
events.description:
Fires when the scene is about to lose its active status, for example when a
system overlay (like the notification center) covers the scene or when the
user switches to another scene. This is the per-scene equivalent of the
legacy [pause](Titanium.App.iOS.pause) event and mirrors
[Titanium.UI.Window.blur](api:Titanium.UI.Window#blur) at the scene level.

Add a listener via `scene.addEventListener('blur', fn)`.

properties.name: sceneId
properties.summary: The unique identifier of the scene.

properties.name: scene
properties.summary: The scene proxy that is resigning active.

events.name: focus
events.summary: Fired when this scene becomes active and can receive user input.
events.description:
Fires when the scene transitions to the active state, meaning it is in the
foreground and receiving user input events. This is the per-scene equivalent
of the legacy [resumed](Titanium.App.iOS.resumed) event and mirrors
[Titanium.UI.Window.focus](api:Titanium.UI.Window#focus) at the scene level.

Add a listener via `scene.addEventListener('focus', fn)`. The
listener fires only for this scene, not for other scenes in the app.

properties.name: sceneId
properties.summary: The unique identifier of the scene.

properties.name: scene
properties.summary: The scene proxy that became active.

events.name: paused
events.summary: Fired when this scene has entered the background.
events.description:
Fires when the scene is no longer visible on screen. This can happen when
the user switches to another app or when the scene is dismissed. This is
the per-scene equivalent of the legacy [paused](Titanium.App.iOS.paused)
event.

Add a listener via `scene.addEventListener('paused', fn)`.

properties.name: sceneId
properties.summary: The unique identifier of the scene.

properties.name: scene
properties.summary: The scene proxy that entered the background.

events.name: resumed
events.summary: Fired when this scene is about to enter the foreground.
events.description:
Fires when the scene transitions from the background to the foreground,
meaning it becomes visible on screen but may not yet be active. This is
the per-scene equivalent of the legacy [resume](Titanium.App.iOS.resume)
event.

Add a listener via `scene.addEventListener('resumed', fn)`.

properties.name: sceneId
properties.summary: The unique identifier of the scene.

properties.name: scene
properties.summary: The scene proxy that is entering the foreground.
